title: Install convergence checklist and sleuth notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working doc for rapid field troubleshooting during VPC/on-prem installer convergence and runtime issues. Focus is on the fast probes we run during an install or upgrade that hangs, partially applies, or has degraded runtime behavior. Treat as a living checklist + sleuth notebook — short commands, observable signatures, hypothesis->probe mappings, and quick rollback/mitigation actions.

Audience:
- First responders on on-prem/VPC installs (SEs, SRE on-call, Solutions Eng)
- Runbook for upgrade canaries and small rollouts

Guiding principles (short):
- Probe with minimal blast radius first (read-only queries, logs, TCP connectivity).
- Prefer deterministic checks that reduce hypothesis space quickly.
- Record a single failing step and its timestamp (correlate with telemetry).
- If terraform plan/apply stalls for >10m, snapshot state + escalate.

Quick summary checklist (0-10 min):
1) Control plane reachability
  - curl -fS --connect-timeout 5 https://CONTROL_PLANE_IP:8443/health || note HTTP code and RTT
  - ping DNS name and ip: nslookup <control-name> ; dig +short <control-name>
2) SSH & node health
  - ssh to a node, check top, free -h, df -h /var/lib | journalctl -u lighthouse.service -n 200 --no-pager
3) Terraform locking & state
  - terraform plan (in module dir) to detect conflicts; check remote state lock: terraform state list || aws s3api get-object --bucket TFSTATE --key key.json (or check consul/remote backend)
4) K8s pivot checks
  - kubectl get nodes -o wide ; kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide
5) GPU driver sanity (if GPUs present)
  - nvidia-smi -L ; dmesg | grep -i nvrm ; gpu-burn or simple inference smoke to validate driver/kernel combo
6) Network MTU and path MTU
  - ip link show ; ip route ; iperf3 between nodes; check BGP sessions for VPC installs
7) Image pull & registry auth
  - docker pull <image> ; crictl pull <image> ; check registry logs and creds in secret
8) Time sync and certs
  - chronyc tracking or timedatectl ; openssl s_client -connect CONTROL_PLANE_IP:8443 -showcerts

Deeper probes and evidence collection (10-40 min)
- Terraform partial apply symptoms: stuck on resource X, apply logs show 409/429/timeout. Probe: check provider plugin logs (~/.terraform.d/plugins), API limits for cloud provider, and examine tfstate object for partial resources. Command: jq '.' terraform.tfstate | head -n 120
- Network blackhole: some nodes curl control-plane but others get timeout. Probe: traceroute -n <control-ip> ; iperf3 server/client with --json to capture throughput; check CNI logs (calico/flannel) and kube-proxy logs.
- Pod crash loops only after upgrade: check image digests changed vs pinned SHA, sidecar incompatibilities. kubectl describe pod && kubectl logs --previous -c main.
- Kubelet timeouts on scheduling: kubelet journal shows image pull backoff vs disk pressure. free -m and lsblk to confirm ephemeral device usage.
- TF apply OOM of provider plugin: check kernel dmesg, system OOM killer logs (journalctl -k), and increase provider memory or split apply.

Terraform module notes (practical tips):
- Keep state mutation idempotent: prefer create_before_destroy for resources that can cause long drains.
- When upgrading modules, add intermediate compatibility versions in the plan to avoid large diffs for cloud resources.
- Use short, targeted applies for bootstrap resources (VPC, subnets, storage) then a separate apply for compute/runtime. This reduces blast radius on retries.
- Enable detailed logging for the provider with TF_LOG=DEBUG for a failed run and collect the output (rotate/compress).
- Check for provider rate-limits: add retry_backoff or split apply into smaller chunks.

Upgrade plan quick template (canary-first):
- Stage 0: Preflight (automated checks)
  - Run preflight script: ./scripts/preflight.sh --target <cluster> (checks image availability, node capacity, driver versions, registry creds)
  - Snapshot tfstate and k8s manifests: gsutil/azcopy/cp to secure artifact store
- Stage 1: Canary (1 node or small shard)
  - Apply new runtime image/helm chart to canary pool (label nodes: redwood-canary=true)
  - Run smoke CI that includes 100 short inferences, embedding tests, and a 5-minute latency/throughput monitor
- Stage 2: Gradual rollout (10-30%)
  - Increase rollout with health gating: CPU, memory, error rate, 95p latency, model accuracy regression checks
- Stage 3: Full rollout and stabilization
  - Monitor for 24-48 hours at production QPS to capture rare flakes

Typical failure signatures -> quick hypothesis map:
- "Installer hung during tf apply with repeated API 429s" -> provider rate limits / credential scope / concurrent applies. Probe: cloud provider API metrics, reduce parallelism, add retries.
- "Pods not scheduling after node join" -> taint/toleration mismatch, insufficient resources, or Kubelet auth. Probe: kubectl describe node ; check kube-proxy and certs.
- "Control plane 502/504" -> ingress/load-balancer or gateway health checks failing; curl LB directly and compare.
- "Inference latency spikes after upgrade" -> model binary mismatch, quantized backend change, or kernel scheduling. Probe: run regression suite on pinned model version and compare histograms.

Command snippets we actually use (keep handy):
- snapshot tf state: aws s3 cp s3://tfstate/prod/cluster.tfstate ./backups/cluster.tfstate.$(date -u +%s)
- quick pod failures: kubectl get pods -A --no-headers | awk '{if($3!~/Running|Completed/) print $0}'
- check for OOMs: journalctl -k | grep -i oom ; grep -i kill /var/log/syslog || dmesg | grep -i oom
- registry auth test: curl -u $REG_USER:$REG_PASS -I https://registry.example.com/v2/

Telemetry & alert sanity assertions (run post-upgrade):
- 95p latency should not regress >20% within 1 hour of rollout
- error-rate (500s/timeout) must remain <0.5% for baseline traffic
- token-per-request cost delta within expected band (no silent token explosion)
- embed/coldstart cache hit rate should remain stable (if caching enabled)

Escalation & rollback playbook (fast mitigations):
1) If control-plane is down for >5min: fail traffic to previous region/replica and switch LB; rollback runtime image to previous manifest and re-apply; create incident channel and pin tfstate snapshot.
2) If tf apply partially succeeded and resources are inconsistent: avoid re-run apply with same plan until state is snapshotted. Create an annotation of the partial resource id to ticket. If safe, terraform destroy the partial resource and re-run.
3) If nodes show kernel-driver mismatch and GPUs unhealthy: cordon affected nodes, drain, deprovision and recreate with matching AMI/kernel/driver.

Notes-to-self / common gotchas we've hit before:
- MTU mismatch with corporate routers + vpc-peering can silently drop gRPC streams; always test with MTU-sized TCP streams, not only ping.
- Kube-proxy iptables rules can persist during upgrades if the node reboots and iptables-manager service is still running stale; restart kube-proxy and ensure conntrack entries are cleared.
- TF partial apply leaves provider locks in cloud provider console — manually clear after confirming no active apply.
- Container runtimes: crictl and docker may show different image lists if CRI shim is misconfigured. Use the runtime used by k8s (check kubelet --container-runtime-endpoint).

Section: Quick evidence capture template (copy into incident ticket)
- Timestamp: <UTC ts>
- Short symptom: e.g., "tf apply hang on aws_ecs_service.redwood-runtime"
- Last terraform line: <copy last 10 lines>
- Node delta: kubectl get nodes -o wide (snapshot)
- TF state snapshot SHA256: <sha> and link to s3/gs
- Key logs: lighthouse.service journal tail, kubelet journal tail, relevant pod logs with -n flag
- Preliminary hypothesis (1 sentence) and next probe planned

Followups (to formalize into runbook):
- Convert the preflight script into a health-check operator that emits Prometheus metrics we can scrape during upgrades
- Add TF sanity guardrails that detect drift before upgrade and refuse large diffs unless forced
- Add a lightweight remote-run sandbox to replay failed tf apply in an isolated account for root cause reproduction

Appendix: Useful references and command cheat-sheet
- scripts/preflight.sh (repo internal)
- GH PR link: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/149
- Jira tickets: PD-4283 (vpc convergence), INFRA-912 (provider retry tuning)

-- end working notes --

(If you copy ANY of this into a public facing runbook, please remove shorthand and include full commands/credentials references; this is a living internal doc with partial notes and assumptions.)
